newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end lower despite SBI's gains.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end lower despite SBI's gains.

text.p: Delhi shares drifted quietly to a lower close as buying interest in the State Bank of India (SBI) following approval of its Euro issue failed to offset profit-taking and selling by foreign investors, brokers said.
The Delhi bourse's benchmark index closed 4.04 points lower at 742.65.

The Indian government on Friday approved a proposal by the State Bank of India (SBI) to raise $500 million through global depositary receipts (GDRs). The state-owned bank said it planned to raise only $400 million through the issue.
SBI bucked the trend, adding 1.05 rupees to 264.65, well off the session high of 269.
Brokers said political turmoil in the western state of Gujarat discouraged buyers.
On Thursday, President Shankar Dayal Sharma dismissed the government in Gujarat after Hindu nationalists ruling the state won a trust vote marred by violence.

The right-wing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party accused the centre-left federal government of trying to gain a political advantage ahead of local polls at the end of the month in populous Uttar Pradesh state.
The sacking of the Gujarat government raised political tension, unnerving investors, brokers said.
Reliance Industries ended 0.70 rupee lower at 197.80 while TISCO lose 0.45 rupee to 175.80.
ACC fell 21 rupees to 1,872 and TELCO shed 2.60 rupees to close at 140.50.
Oriental Bank of Commerce fell 0.35 rupee to close at 70.
